newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietsovpetro oil output seen up 22.4 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Vietsovpetro oil output seen up 22.4 pct in 1996.

text.p: Vietsovpetro's oil output is expected to rise by 1.5 million tonnes, or 22.4 percent, to 8.2 million this year and then jump again in 1997 to 9.0 million tonnes, state media reports said on Friday.
The official daily Nhan Dan said Vietsovpetro, a Vietnamese-Russian joint venture, was expected to have turnover of $1.2 billion this year.

Vietsovpetro produces the bulk of Vietnam's oil, with other companies accounting for around one million tonnes of combined output of 7.7 million tonnes last year. Most of the country's oil comes from the Bach Ho (White Tiger) field off the coast of Vietnam and is exported for refining.
The daily Vietnam News said nearly 7.0 million tonnes had been exported from the White Tiger in the first 10-1/2 months of this year.
Vietnam is planning to produce 20 million tonnes of crude oil per year by 2000 and increase annual output to between 30 and 40 million tonnes during the next decade.
